CTAs ``. signupUrl = `https://inkos.up.railway.app/signup`.** --- ## PAGE 1: `/migrate/mangomint` **`src/app/migrate/mangomint/layout.tsx`:** ```ts import type { Metadata } from "next"; export const metadata: Metadata = { title: "Migrate from Mangomint to InkOS — 6-day move, tattoo-native | InkOS", description: "Mangomint is salon-coded. InkOS is tattoo-native. Multi-session projects, deposit pools, allergy intelligence — concepts Mangomint doesn't have. 6-day white-glove migration.", openGraph: { title: "Migrate from Mangomint to InkOS", description: "Salon software is built for haircuts. Tattoo deserves better.", type: "website" }, alternates: { canonical: "https://inkos.studio/migrate/mangomint" }, }; export default function Layout({ children }: Readonly<{ children: React.ReactNode }>) { return children; } ``` **`src/app/migrate/mangomint/page.tsx`:** **Hero:** ```tsx ``` **The architectural difference** (GRADIENT.sectionCool, paddingTop 100 paddingBottom 100): SectionEyebrow "Why architecture matters" accent="rust" + h2 "Tattoo-native, from the first commit." size sm. 3 MoatCardBright-style cards (rust/amber/sage): 1. (rust, LayoutGrid) "Multi-session projects, native" — "Mangomint treats every booking as a transaction. InkOS groups them: a sleeve is one project, four sessions, one deposit pool. The whole work, in one place." Detail: [Mangomint: per-booking] [InkOS: per-project] [Built for: tattoo workflow] 2. (amber, AlertCircle) "Allergy intelligence, surfaces" — "Mangomint stores notes. InkOS surfaces the red ink allergy on Today, on the schedule card, in the artist's brief — three places, one source." Detail: [Mangomint: notes field] [InkOS: 4-place surface] [Risk: managed] 3. (sage, DollarSign) "Deposit pool accounting" — "Mangomint deposits attach to bookings. Reschedule and the deposit floats. InkOS pools deposits to projects — they travel with the client, not the slot." Detail: [Mangomint: per-booking] [InkOS: per-project pool] [Refund logic: re-balances] **Comparison table:** ```tsx ``` **What we carry** (BRAND.bone, paddingTop 80 paddingBottom 80, SectionEyebrow "What we carry" accent="amber" + h2 "Every record migrates clean." size sm): 3 cards (same MoatCardBright pattern as above): 1. "Every client" — "Names, contacts, notes, custom fields. Mangomint custom fields become InkOS Notes or get promoted to first-class fields." 2. "Every booking" — "Future appointments, recurring bookings, blocked time. The Mangomint calendar = the InkOS calendar at cutover." 3. "Every transaction" — "Outstanding deposits, completed payments, refunds. Stripe Connect re-attached. Money state preserved." **6-day plan** (GRADIENT.sectionWarm, SectionEyebrow "6-day plan" accent="rust" + h2 "How Mangomint studios migrate." size sm): Timeline: - Day 1: Discovery + Mangomint API access - Day 2-3: Export + clean - Day 4: Schema mapping (salon → tattoo concepts: tip jar → deposit pool, package → project, etc.) - Day 5: Preview run + sign-off - Day 6: Cutover + cancel Mangomint **Customer quote** (use any from `/customers` — for variety, use Tomas Bel): ```tsx ``` **FAQ:** - "Mangomint's customer support is great. Does InkOS match?" — "Different model. Mangomint has a big support org for a wide audience. We have engineers + a small team for tattoo studios specifically. Email response under 24h on every plan, chat under 4h on Pro." - "Will my packages convert to InkOS projects?" — "Yes. Mangomint packages map to InkOS multi-session projects. Discounts, scheduled sessions, prepaid deposits — all carry." - "Does InkOS support tip jars?" — "Yes — though we treat them as a tip line on the invoice rather than a separate jar. Tips route to artists via Stripe Connect." - "Can I run InkOS alongside Mangomint during migration?" — "Yes. Standard parallel run for 14 days. We don't bill until you cancel Mangomint." - "What if my staff is used to Mangomint's UI?" — "Most teams transition in 2-3 days. We do a remote training session on day 5 of migration. Includes recording for new hires." **CTA:** ```tsx ``` --- ## PAGE 2: `/reach-compliance` **`src/app/reach-compliance/layout.tsx`:** ```ts import type { Metadata } from "next"; export const metadata: Metadata = { title: "EU REACH Compliance for Tattoo Studios | InkOS", description: "EU REACH 2022 compliance for tattoo studios. Ink registry, MSDS attachments, batch tracking, reaction logging, inspector reports. Built into InkOS Inventory.", openGraph: { title: "REACH compliance, built in", description: "EU REACH 2022 compliance for tattoo studios.", type: "website" }, alternates: { canonical: "https://inkos.studio/reach-compliance" }, }; export default function Layout({ children }: Readonly<{ children: React.ReactNode }>) { return children; } ``` **`src/app/reach-compliance/page.tsx`:** **Hero:** ```tsx ``` **What is REACH section** (GRADIENT.sectionWarm, paddingTop 100 paddingBottom 100): SectionEyebrow "Background" accent="rust" + h2 "What REACH 2022 means for your studio." size sm. Long-form prose (white card maxWidth 720, padding 32, SHADOW.soft): - p1: "REACH (Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals) is the EU regulation governing chemical substances. The 2022 amendment (Annex XVII, entry 75) restricts specific pigments and additives in tattoo and permanent makeup inks." - p2: "If you operate in any EU member state, your inks must comply. Bottles must list CI numbers. MSDS sheets must be on file. Reactions must be logged. Inspectors can ask, and 'we have it on a spreadsheet' is no longer a defensible answer." - p3: "InkOS treats compliance as a feature, not a checkbox. Every bottle in your inventory has a CI number, batch ID, MSDS attachment, and shelf-life tracking. Reactions are logged on both the client AND the bottle batch. Reports export in one click for inspectors." **The 4 pillars section** (BRAND.bone, paddingTop 100 paddingBottom 100, SectionEyebrow "Four compliance pillars" accent="amber" + h2 "What InkOS automates." size sm): 4 cards in 2x2 grid (rust/amber/sage/rust): 1. (rust, Shield) "CI number registry" — "Every ink in your cabinet linked to its CI number. Validated against the EU REACH 2022 ink registry. Prohibited substances flagged red." Detail: [Validation: against REACH registry] [Flagging: prohibited subs] [Update cycle: quarterly] 2. (amber, FileText) "MSDS attachments" — "Material Safety Data Sheets attached to every bottle. PDF, expirable, version-tracked. Inspector pulls the report, the MSDS comes with it." Detail: [Format: PDF] [Storage: Supabase] [Audit: version history] 3. (sage, AlertCircle) "Reaction logging" — "Client reacts to red ink? Logged on the client AND the bottle batch. Future studios using the same batch see the warning. Network-wide intelligence." Detail: [Per-client: yes] [Per-batch: yes] [Cross-studio: opt-in] 4. (rust, BarChart3) "Inspector reports" — "One click exports a PDF: every bottle, every CI, every MSDS, every reaction. Quarterly or on-demand. Submitted to the inspector before they leave." Detail: [Export format: PDF] [Generation time: <30s] [Retention: 7 years] Use grid `repeat(2, 1fr)` with className `reach-pillars-grid` and a ` ``` ## Icons to import - /migrate/mangomint: ArrowRight, LayoutGrid, AlertCircle, DollarSign - /reach-compliance: ArrowRight, Shield, FileText, AlertCircle, BarChart3 ## Verification After all 4 files: `cd "/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Marketing Site/InkOS" && pnpm run type-check`.
